newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee calls news conference.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee calls news conference.

text.p: Maine Yankee, owners of the 910 megawatt (MW) Maine Yankee nuclear power plant, have called a news conference for 1400 EST/1900 GMT Friday.

The company declined to comment on the purpose of the news conference, but its announcement raised speculation the plant, already shut amid safety concerns, might be closed longer than earlier anticipated.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), whose concerns over improperly laid cabling led to the current outage, said in its daily report Friday that the plant's operators "will decide today if cooldown is necessary."

A cooldown would involve fully shutting the plant's reactor. A similar move was made at the Connecticut Yankee power station ahead of its owners' decision last month to permanently shut the unit for economic reasons.

Asked if permanently closing Maine Yankee was a likely scenario, Diane Screnci, spokeswoman at the NRC's regional northeast office in Pennsylvania, replied "As an agency, we don't see why the plant (Maine Yankee) can't restart.
"That would be their decision whether to shut the plant or to invest more money to fix the problems" she said.

Maine Yankee officials said Thursday that they planned to present a thorough review of the cabling problems to the NRC before restarting the plant, adding the review likely would take about three weeks.
The plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, was shut December 6 when workers discovered two improperly installed electrical cables in the reactor control system that did not meet the plant's safety requirements.
The cables serve the reactor trip breakers which are used to shut the plant manually or automatically.
Maine Yankee also said earlier this month that it planed to spend about $27 million in 1997 to address safety concerns at the 24-year-old plant, including hiring 50 new workers.
Maine Yankee is operated by Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co.

It is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
